subject: The Papyrus · Hollywood on the Nile
html:
The Arab world watched itself through Egyptian eyes

For most of the twentieth century, when the Arab world went to the cinema, it watched Egyptian films. Egypt has produced more than 4,000 feature films — historically the majority of all Arab film output — and by the 1950s its industry was, by some accounts, the third largest in the world, behind only Hollywood and Bombay. (Sources: Cinema of Egypt; Al-Ahram.)

The Golden Age, and its stars

The Golden Age (1930s–1960s) gave the region a shared screen language and stars it still reveres: Faten Hamama, the leading lady of the era; Youssef Chahine, a director honoured at Berlin and Cannes; and Omar Sharif, who went from Cairo to Lawrence of Arabia and Doctor Zhivago — Egypt's global film star. Cairo's accent became the accent everyone in the Arab world could understand, largely because of these films.

Still the box office

It isn't only history. In 2025 the Egyptian box office recovered past pre-COVID levels — about EGP 1.8bn on ~14 million admissions — and here's the striking split: Egyptian films are only about 20% of the titles on screens but roughly 70% of the money, with 8 of the year's top 10 home-grown. (Source: ScreenDaily, 2025.) A small share of the catalogue, most of the audience — a reminder that counting titles and counting tickets tell two very different stories.
